verdict.rationale: The IRS publishes the EIN online assistant, a founder's core online flow, as a single-session tool with operating hours. It expires after 15 minutes of inactivity with no save, which implies session-based entry without a pre-created account. However, no cited page explicitly states that no account is needed. Other online rails, such as signed mobile-friendly forms including the 83(b) Form 15620, do require an ID.me-verified Online Account. Missing for 10: an explicit published statement that the EIN assistant needs no account or login, a documented keyless or file-number entry step, and hands-on confirmation of account-free entry.

support.subject: As a founder, I can start the core online flow without creating an account first — the service's published pages document a keyless or file-number entry path

citations.quote: It expires after 15 minutes of inactivity, and you'll need to start over.
This tool is available during the following times (Eastern Time): Mon–Fri: 6:00 a.m. – 1:00 a.m. (next day)
You can apply for only 1 EIN per responsible party per day.
